title: Google Elephant-Goldfish Plugin Enforces Spec-First Coding
summary: Google's Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin makes coding agents draft specifications first, then runs five zero-context review stages before writing code.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Google officially released the Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin on November 8, 2026, requiring coding agents to draft complete specifications before generating code.
- The plugin runs five independent zero-context review stages to validate specifications, ensuring no assumptions carry forward from earlier analysis.
- This spec-first approach aims to reduce technical debt and improve code quality by catching design flaws before implementation begins.


Google AI has officially launched the Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin, a development tool that fundamentally restructures how[coding agents](https://emergent.sh/glossary/coding-agent) approach software development. Officially released on November 8, 2026, the plugin mandates that agents draft complete specifications before writing any code, then subjects those specs to five sequential zero-context review stages designed to eliminate assumption drift and catch design flaws early.


## How the Five-Stage Review Process Works


The Elephant-Goldfish plugin enforces a strict separation between specification and implementation. When a coding agent receives a development task, it must first produce a detailed specification document outlining architecture, data flows, edge cases, and acceptance criteria. The plugin then launches five independent review stages, each operating with zero context from previous stages to prevent confirmation bias.


Each review stage receives only the specification document and a narrow evaluation mandate: one checks logical consistency, another validates edge case coverage, a third assesses security implications, a fourth reviews scalability assumptions, and a fifth examines testability. Only after all five stages approve the spec does the plugin permit code generation. According to Google, this approach reduces rework cycles by catching architectural problems before they become embedded in code.


## Zero-Context Validation Architecture


The plugin's defining feature is its zero-context review methodology. Traditional code review tools accumulate context as they analyze a project, potentially carrying forward flawed assumptions. Elephant-Goldfish deliberately strips context between review stages, forcing each validator to evaluate the specification independently based solely on the document's internal logic and explicit statements.


This architecture mirrors how different team members with specialized knowledge might review a design document without conferring. The plugin uses separate model instances for each review stage, with no shared memory or state. Google reports this design catches 3x more specification errors compared to single-pass reviews in internal testing.


## Integration with Existing Coding Agents


The Elephant-Goldfish plugin integrates with popular coding agent frameworks through a standard API. Developers can configure the plugin to enforce spec-first workflows in continuous integration pipelines, blocking code commits that lack approved specifications. The plugin supports custom review criteria, allowing teams to add domain-specific validators for compliance, performance budgets, or accessibility requirements.


Google has released the plugin as an open-source tool with adapters for GitHub Copilot, Cursor, and standalone[AI coding assistants](https://emergent.sh/glossary/coding-assistant) . Early adopters report longer initial development cycles offset by dramatically reduced debugging time and technical debt accumulation. The plugin maintains an audit trail of all specification versions and review outcomes, providing documentation for regulatory compliance and team knowledge transfer.


## Release Date and Availability


Google officially launched the Elephant-Goldfish Model plugin on November 8, 2026, with immediate availability through the company's AI development tools repository. The plugin requires no proprietary Google infrastructure and runs locally on developer machines or in self-hosted CI/CD environments. Documentation includes migration guides for teams transitioning from code-first to spec-first workflows.


## What This Means for Software Development


The Elephant-Goldfish plugin represents a significant shift in how AI coding tools operate, prioritizing design validation over rapid code generation. By forcing specification clarity before implementation, the tool addresses a common criticism of coding agents: their tendency to generate syntactically correct but architecturally flawed code. As more development teams adopt[agentic coding](https://emergent.sh/glossary/agentic-coding) workflows, tools that embed quality gates directly into the generation process may become standard practice, reshaping expectations around AI-assisted development speed versus long-term maintainability.
